![ZotFlag infographic](zotflag-infographic.png)

It is a Zotero extension (for Zotero 7 to 10) that automatically adds
tags to selected references when their metadata matches lists kept in
CSV files.

- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/pmartinolli/ZotFlag)
- [Discussion, application and empirical
  analysis](https://pmartinolli.github.io/blog/2026/ZotFlag/) (in
  French).

+------------------+------------------------+
| CSV filenames    | Matching Zotero fields |
+==================+========================+
| `keywords.csv`   | Tags (strict)          |
|                  |                        |
|                  | Title                  |
|                  |                        |
|                  | Abstract               |
+------------------+------------------------+
| `journals.csv`   | Publication            |
+------------------+------------------------+
| `journals.csv`   | ISSN                   |
+------------------+------------------------+
| `persons.csv`    | author                 |
|                  |                        |
|                  | editor                 |
+------------------+------------------------+
| `publishers.csv` | Publisher              |
+------------------+------------------------+
| `dois.csv`       | DOI                    |
+------------------+------------------------+
| `urls.csv`       | URL                    |
+------------------+------------------------+

« Make it so. » was a catchphrase written by Gene Roddenberry,
[inspired](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/make_it_so) by the British
naval officers of the XIXe century. It was first used in "Encounter At
Farpoint" (28 September 1987) and then reused with much delight by
Captain Jean-Luc Picard (*In memoriam*) during the run of
[ST:TNG](https://www.startrek.com/en-ca/videos/make-it-so-captain-picard)
1987-1994.
